knowledge.title: Quadratic Equation Solver
knowledge.content: A quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0 has solutions x = (-b ± √(b²-4ac)) / 2a. The discriminant Δ = b²-4ac determines the nature of roots: Δ > 0 → two real roots, Δ = 0 → one repeated root, Δ < 0 → two complex conjugate roots.

knowledge.title: System of Linear Equations
knowledge.content: A system of linear equations can be solved using Gaussian elimination, matrix inversion, or Cramer's rule. For Ax = b, if A is invertible: x = A⁻¹b. Gaussian elimination transforms the augmented matrix [A|b] to row-echelon form.

knowledge.title: Derivative Rules
knowledge.content: Common derivative rules: d/dx(xⁿ) = nxⁿ⁻¹ (power rule), d/dx(eˣ) = eˣ, d/dx(ln x) = 1/x, d/dx(sin x) = cos x, d/dx(cos x) = -sin x. Chain rule: d/dx(f(g(x))) = f'(g(x))·g'(x). Product rule: d/dx(fg) = f'g + fg'. Quotient rule: d/dx(f/g) = (f'g - fg')/g².

knowledge.title: Integration Rules
knowledge.content: Common integrals: ∫xⁿdx = xⁿ⁺¹/(n+1) + C (n≠-1), ∫eˣdx = eˣ + C, ∫(1/x)dx = ln|x| + C, ∫sin x dx = -cos x + C, ∫cos x dx = sin x + C. Integration by parts: ∫udv = uv - ∫vdu. Substitution rule: ∫f(g(x))g'(x)dx = ∫f(u)du where u = g(x).

knowledge.title: Prime Numbers and Factorization
knowledge.content: A prime number is a natural number > 1 with no positive divisors other than 1 and itself. Sieve of Eratosthenes finds all primes up to n in O(n log log n). Fundamental theorem of arithmetic: every integer > 1 has a unique prime factorization. Fermat's little theorem: if p is prime and gcd(a,p)=1, then a^(p-1) ≡ 1 (mod p).

knowledge.title: Mean, Variance, and Standard Deviation
knowledge.content: Mean (μ) = Σxᵢ/n. Variance (σ²) = Σ(xᵢ-μ)²/n. Standard deviation (σ) = √variance. For sample data, use n-1 denominator (Bessel's correction). These measure central tendency and spread of data.

knowledge.title: Permutations and Combinations
knowledge.content: Permutations P(n,r) = n!/(n-r)!: number of ways to arrange r items from n. Combinations C(n,r) = n!/(r!(n-r)!): number of ways to choose r items from n without regard to order. Binomial theorem: (a+b)ⁿ = ΣC(n,k)·aⁿ⁻ᵏ·bᵏ.
